2) Hosting preference: Hosted API vs Dedicated reserved capacity vs Private VPC (Daniel noted data residency/regulatory constraints).

I've attached two artifacts to accelerate internal review: pricing_options_v2.pdf (tiered commit vs on-demand matrix) and redwood_maas_T&Cs_v3.docx. They cover our standard commercial constructs and a sample PO invoice flow.

Immediate next steps we recommend:
- You confirm purchasing preference (PO vs card vs marketplace) and ideal timeline for legal signoff.

- If Private VPC: we will include a DPA and SOC2 evidence in the package (attaching SOC2 + DPA once I confirm).
- Redwood to deliver an initial SOW + quote reflecting your hosting preference and commit level (we can draft a committed 12-month tier and an on-demand baseline for comparison).

Can we block 30 minutes on Thurs to walk through the options and a draft quote? I propose Thu 08/17 10:00 PT — happy to move.

Marissa — thanks for the clear notes. Couple quick answers from procurement side:

• Purchasing preference: our default is PO (corporate purchasing card only for < $2k ad-hoc). Marketplace participation is possible but needs procurement approval; it often expedites purchase if price/terms are equivalent.
• Billing cadence: Net30 is our standard.
• Legal review: expect 2-3 weeks for a standard SaaS agreement; for any additional security addenda (DPA) it may add another week.
• PO owner: procurement@bluegrain.com (cc'd). They will issue the PO once a final quote + SOW are approved.

We are leaning toward Dedicated (reserved capacity) for production if commit economics make sense, but Daniel will confirm the data handling needs for dev vs prod.

Please send a draft SOW and a committed vs on-demand comparison. If you can include a marketplace SKU for comparison, that would be helpful so procurement can evaluate speed to PO vs approved marketplace purchase.

Thanks —
Susan Park
VP, Procurement | Bluegrain Analytics
susan@bluegrain.com

Thanks team — a few technical clarifications from engineering that will influence hosting choice:

• Data sensitivity: production will process pseudonymized PII and customer IDs. We prefer Private VPC for production if there are minimal networking overheads; Dedicated reserved capacity (single-tenant within cloud region) is acceptable if we can get a contractual guarantee around KV cache isolation and audit logs.
• Compliance artifacts: we will need your current SOC 2 report and a DPA to start legal review. Please attach SOC2 and a DPA template.
• Timeline: engineering and security will review the SOC2 and respond in ~5 business days. Procurement will then start legal redlines.

PO vs marketplace: procurement to weigh in, but if marketplace shortens procurement lead time by >2 weeks we may favor it for initial proof-of-concept, with Dedicated/Private for production.

— Daniel Ruiz
